terms.comment: Priscian’s Greek word (σύνταξις). Traupman’s pupil answers how he knows a case: Ā syntaxī, from the syntax (239).
Classically a building or arrangement; Cicero’s phrase for the arrangement of words is cōnfōrmātiō verbōrum (de Or. 1.151, Lewis & Short).
Traupman offers it as the “pure Latin” word; Lewis & Short gives it of order and arrangement in general (Vitruvius, Pliny), not of words.

phrases.latin: Unde hoc certum est? — Ā syntaxī.
phrases.english: How is that certain? — From the syntax.

ordinatio.html: From ōrdō, which Lewis & Short marks long.
